content_of_post_to_comment:
Among all the other issues that not using social media brings (Fomo, a sense of loneliness, etc.) one of the biggest hurdles is that it feels like its basically impossible to exist at the same frequency of your peers when you aren't actively using social media. you miss everything. every reference, every plan, every piece of news, etc.

I'm finding it much harder to meet new people or retain friends. It's like you don't even exist a lot of the time. I don't know if this problem is exacerbated by the fact im in my early twenties but it feels insurmountable sometimes.

I already feel lonely, the lack of connection is making me feel lonelier and on top of that, not using social media makes me feel even lonelier (although i know that using it will only give me a fake sense of gratification and ultimately ill feel worse) but still I think its worth bringing up.

is it just a necessary evil I have to accept? that I will need to maintain social media in some form? I wish I could just live with a flip phone or something and have that not be contested or bring me any issues.
comment: I think the hard part is that social media has quietly become an infrastructure layer for friendships, not just entertainment. But there’s a difference between being disconnected and being absent. Some people I know barely post but stay connected through group chats, hobbies, classes, or regular plans. The tricky part might be replacing the “ambient awareness” social media gives you with more intentional ways of showing up.
